metadata.spec_revision: spec_update_3 (VLSIT instance names in section 6); parameters renamed PR_* to PARA_* to match the released RTL (verification owner, 2026-10-19)
metadata.description: AXI4 (full) slave controller that bridges one AXI4 master to one or more synchronous SRAM banks with one-cycle read latency, using per-channel FIFOs, two address FSMs and a shared round-robin read/write arbiter, with optional XOR-hashed multi-bank operation.

requirements.text: The design shall use a single clock domain i_clk; all sequential state shall change only on the rising edge of i_clk or on assertion of i_rst_n.
i_rst_n shall be an active-low reset with asynchronous assertion; its deassertion shall be synchronous to i_clk (synchronizer outside the block).
The AXI write address channel shall consist of i_awaddr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], i_awvalid, o_awready, i_awburst[1:0], i_awlen[PARA_LEN_WD-1:0], i_awid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0] and i_awsize[2:0].
The AXI write data channel shall consist of i_wdata[PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], i_wstrb[PARA_DATA_WD/8-1:0], i_wvalid, o_wready and i_wlast.
The AXI write response channel shall consist of o_bid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0], o_bresp[1:0], o_bvalid and i_bready.
The AXI read address channel shall consist of i_araddr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], i_arvalid, o_arready, i_arburst[1:0], i_arlen[PARA_LEN_WD-1:0], i_arid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0] and i_arsize[2:0].
The AXI read data channel shall consist of o_rid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0], o_rdata[PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], o_rresp[1:0], o_rvalid, o_rlast and i_rready; o_rdata shall always carry the full SRAM word.

The SRAM interface shall provide per-bank packed arrays o_sram_addr[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], o_sram_wdata[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], o_sram_wstrb[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD/8-1:0], o_sram_we[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0], o_sram_oe[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0] (active high) and input i_sram_rdata[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD-1:0]; with PARA_NUM_BANKS = 1 it shall be bit-for-bit the single-SRAM interface.

o_awready shall be 1 exactly when the write address FSM is in S_IDLE and AWFIFO is not full (current-cycle flag); o_arready likewise for the read FSM and ARFIFO. Neither shall depend combinationally on the corresponding VALID input, and a FIFO pop in the same cycle shall not raise READY.

o_wready shall equal NOT(WFIFO full) on the current-cycle flag and shall not depend on i_wvalid; {i_wstrb, i_wdata} shall be pushed into WFIFO when i_wvalid & o_wready, and W beats may be accepted before their AW burst.

o_bvalid shall equal NOT(BFIFO empty) and o_bid/o_bresp shall be the BFIFO head entry; once o_bvalid is 1, it and the payload shall stay stable until the cycle where i_bready = 1, when the entry is popped.
o_rvalid shall equal NOT(RFIFO empty) and o_rid/o_rdata/o_rresp/o_rlast shall be the RFIFO head entry; they shall stay stable until popped in a cycle where i_rready = 1.
Response encodings shall be OKAY = 2'b00 and SLVERR = 2'b10; EXOKAY and DECERR shall never be generated on o_bresp or o_rresp.
The controller shall return exactly one B response per accepted AW burst, and exactly AxLEN+1 R beats per accepted AR burst with o_rlast = 1 only on the last beat.
The AXI master shall keep VALID and its payload stable from assertion until the handshake on every AXI input channel (AW, W, AR, and READY-side B/R are not constrained).
The AXI master shall send exactly AWLEN+1 W beats per AW burst, in AW order without write-data interleaving, shall use WRAP lengths of 2, 4, 8 or 16 beats only, and should not use AxBURST = 2'b11.

Each SRAM bank k shall write o_sram_wdata[k] into the byte lanes selected by o_sram_wstrb[k] at word o_sram_addr[k][PARA_ADDR_WD-1:BYTE_LSB] at the rising edge ending a cycle with o_sram_we[k] = 1 (unselected bytes unchanged), and shall present the word addressed in a cycle with o_sram_oe[k] = 1 on i_sram_rdata[k] throughout the following cycle (exactly one-cycle read latency); the low BYTE_LSB address bits are ignored and each bank holds the full addressable range.
In any cycle, o_sram_we[k] and o_sram_oe[k] shall not both be 1 for the same bank k.
The controller shall be an AXI4 slave with independent read and write channels: AW and AR handshakes in the same cycle shall be independent and both accepted when their READYs are 1.

After each pushed beat the address FSM shall keep the next beat address unchanged for FIXED bursts (2'b00) and set it to addr + 2**AxSIZE for INCR bursts (2'b01), using the registered AxSIZE; address arithmetic shall be modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD with no 4 KB boundary check.

For WRAP bursts (2'b10) and reserved AxBURST = 2'b11, the next address shall be addr + size_bytes unless that equals wrap_lower + size_bytes*burst_len, in which case it shall be wrap_lower, where wrap_lower = start_addr & ~(size_bytes*burst_len − 1) and burst_len = AxLEN+1 are computed and latched at the handshake (e.g. 4-beat 32-bit WRAP from 0x88 visits 0x88, 0x8C, 0x80, 0x84). AxBURST = 2'b11 shall not by itself cause SLVERR.

Bursts of AxLEN = 0 to 2**PARA_LEN_WD − 1 (1 to 256 beats at the default) shall be handled completely: the beat counter shall be PARA_LEN_WD+1 bits wide, load AxLEN+1 at the handshake, decrement only while non-zero and never wrap.
Data, address and ID widths shall be configurable through PARA_DATA_WD, PARA_ADDR_WD and PARA_ID_WD; all port, FIFO and internal widths shall be derived from them.

Narrow transfers: AxSIZE shall only change the address stride, the WRAP window and the error check; the SRAM shall always be accessed as a full PARA_DATA_WD word, writes narrowed only by WSTRB and reads returning the full word on o_rdata.

o_sram_wstrb[k] shall equal the WFIFO-head strobe (i_wstrb pass-through) while o_sram_we[k] = 1 and shall be all-zero whenever o_sram_we[k] = 0, including SLVERR beats, non-selected banks, read-only and idle cycles; the controller shall do no other byte masking.

At the AW/AR handshake the address FSM shall set err = 1 if i_axsize > MAX_SIZE or (i_axaddr & (2**i_axsize − 1)) != 0, latch it for the whole burst, attach it to every beat, and still generate all AxLEN+1 beats at a 2**AxSIZE stride; there shall be no sticky error state, so later aligned bursts return OKAY.

For a write burst with err = 1, every beat shall pop AWFIFO and WFIFO normally with o_sram_we and o_sram_wstrb held at 0 (SRAM not modified), and exactly one B response with BRESP = SLVERR and the burst's AWID shall be posted.

For a read burst with err = 1, every beat shall be issued like any other (o_sram_oe asserted), and all AxLEN+1 beats shall be returned with RRESP = SLVERR, the burst's ARID, the SRAM word on o_rdata and o_rlast on the final beat.

The AXI ID shall be preserved end to end: AWID captured at the AW handshake shall be carried in every AWFIFO entry and returned on o_bid; ARID shall be carried in every ARFIFO entry and returned on o_rid with each beat. B responses shall come back in AW acceptance order and R beats in AR acceptance order regardless of ID values (ID reuse allowed).

Each AXI channel shall be buffered by its own m_vlsi_fifo instance of depth PARA_FIFO_DEPTH: AWFIFO {last, err, id, addr} (PARA_ADDR_WD+PARA_ID_WD+2 bits), WFIFO {wstrb, wdata} (PARA_DATA_WD+PARA_DATA_WD/8), ARFIFO {last, err, id, addr} (PARA_ADDR_WD+PARA_ID_WD+2), RFIFO {id, rresp, rdata, last} (PARA_DATA_WD+PARA_ID_WD+3) and BFIFO {id, bresp} (PARA_ID_WD+2).

Each FIFO shall use registered read/write pointers of $clog2(PARA_FIFO_DEPTH)+1 bits wrapping modulo 2*PARA_FIFO_DEPTH; full shall be asserted when the pointer MSBs differ and the lower bits are equal, and empty when the pointers are equal.

A FIFO push while full shall be ignored even if a pop happens in the same cycle; a pop while empty shall be ignored while a simultaneous push is still performed; push and pop together on a FIFO that is neither full nor empty shall both take effect; the head entry shall be output combinationally and a pushed entry shall be visible at the head from the cycle after the push.

The shared arbiter (instance u_vlsi_arbiter of m_vlsi_arbiter) shall grant write when only write requests, read when only read requests, and, when both request, write if arb_toggle = 0 and read if arb_toggle = 1.

There shall be one shared arbiter instance (u_vlsi_arbiter) for all bank configurations; its 1-bit arb_toggle shall reset to 0 and invert exactly once at the end of every cycle in which at least one request is granted (write or read), including PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1 cycles where a write and a read issue to different banks.

When PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1, bank_sel_wr and bank_sel_rd shall be computed every cycle on the AWFIFO and ARFIFO head addresses as addr[BYTE_LSB +: BANK_WD] ^ addr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1 -: BANK_WD]; each beat shall be routed individually, and o_sram_addr[k] shall carry the full un-hashed beat address.

When PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1, w_wr_issue shall be req_write & (bank_conflict ? arbiter write grant : 1) and w_rd_issue shall be req_read & (bank_conflict ? arbiter read grant : 1), with bank_conflict = req_write & req_read & (bank_sel_wr == bank_sel_rd); a write and a read to different banks shall both issue in the same cycle.

When PARA_NUM_BANKS = 1, w_wr_issue shall equal the arbiter write grant and w_rd_issue the arbiter read grant (never both in a cycle), implemented as its own generate branch in m_vlsi_bank_arb that reuses the original grant expressions verbatim.

req_write shall be ~awfifo_empty & ~wfifo_empty & (~awfifo_head.last | ~bfifo_full), so the write of a burst's last beat is not granted while BFIFO is full (a BFIFO pop in the same cycle does not release the hold), while non-last beats continue to issue.

req_read shall be ~arfifo_empty & ~rfifo_full & ~reg_rd_pending, so no read issues while RFIFO is full or a read is pending, and at most one SRAM read is in flight system-wide, even with several banks.
i_wlast shall be accepted but ignored; the address FSM shall track the last beat of each burst.

While i_rst_n = 0 and after reset until the first transaction, both address FSMs shall be in S_IDLE with counter = 0 and latched err = 0, all five FIFOs empty, arb_toggle = 0 and reg_rd_pending = 0; therefore o_awready = o_arready = o_wready = 1 (also during reset), o_bvalid = o_rvalid = 0, and o_sram_we = o_sram_oe = 0, o_sram_addr = 0 and o_sram_wstrb = 0 for every bank.

After reset, o_bid, o_bresp, o_rid, o_rdata, o_rresp, o_rlast and o_sram_wdata shall read 0 (FIFO storage cleared), and a transaction in progress when reset asserts shall be discarded without producing a response.

In the handshake cycle c0 the address FSM shall capture i_axaddr, i_axlen, i_axburst, i_axid and i_axsize, load the beat counter with i_axlen + 1, compute and latch err and the WRAP window, and move to S_ADDR at the end of c0.

In every S_ADDR cycle with counter ≠ 0 and its FIFO not full (current-cycle flag), the address FSM shall push {last, err, id, addr} with last = 1 exactly when counter == 1, decrement the counter and update the address; when the FIFO is full it shall stall with no push and no counter or address change (a same-cycle pop does not allow a push); in the first S_ADDR cycle with counter == 0 it shall push nothing and return to S_IDLE.

In a cycle where w_wr_issue = 1, AWFIFO and WFIFO shall both be popped at the end of the cycle, and bank k = bank_sel_wr (0 when single-bank) shall be driven combinationally with o_sram_addr[k] = AWFIFO head address, o_sram_wdata[k] = WFIFO head data and o_sram_we[k] = 1 unless the AWFIFO head err = 1; W beats shall pair with AW beat entries strictly in FIFO order.
When a write issues with AWFIFO head last = 1, {id, err ? SLVERR : OKAY} shall be pushed into BFIFO at the end of that cycle.

In a cycle t where w_rd_issue = 1, o_sram_oe[k] = 1 and o_sram_addr[k] = ARFIFO head address for k = bank_sel_rd, ARFIFO shall be popped at the end of t, and reg_rd_pending shall be set with the head's id, last, err and the bank index captured.
In cycle t+1 after a read issue, {id, err ? SLVERR : OKAY, i_sram_rdata[reg_rd_bank_d], last} shall be pushed into RFIFO (always succeeding) and reg_rd_pending shall clear at the end of t+1.
o_sram_addr[k] shall be 0 in any cycle where bank k has neither o_sram_we[k] nor o_sram_oe[k] asserted, and o_sram_wdata[k] is don't-care while o_sram_we[k] = 0.

FIFO pushes and pops shall never overflow or underflow: address FSMs push only when their FIFO is not full, W is accepted only when WFIFO is not full, the last write beat is held off while BFIFO is full, a read issues only when RFIFO is not full and no read is pending, and B/R pops happen only on handshake.

The design hierarchy shall be kept as prescribed, with instance names per the VLSIT rule u_vlsi_<function>[_<index>]: m_vlsi_axi4_sram instantiates u_vlsi_axfsm_0 (AW) and u_vlsi_axfsm_1 (AR) of m_vlsi_axfsm, u_vlsi_fifo_0..4 of m_vlsi_fifo (0 = AWFIFO, 1 = WFIFO, 2 = ARFIFO, 3 = RFIFO, 4 = BFIFO), u_vlsi_arbiter of m_vlsi_arbiter and u_vlsi_sram_misc of m_vlsi_sram_misc, which instantiates u_vlsi_axi_fifopack, u_vlsi_bank_arb and u_vlsi_sram_fanout; the split of m_vlsi_sram_misc shall cause no change in behaviour or timing.

With no contention and W data already in WFIFO, the first beat of an AW/AR burst handshaken in c0 shall be pushed at the end of c1 and visible at the FIFO head in c2, so the first o_sram_we / o_sram_oe occurs no earlier than c2; a W beat handshaken in cycle n shall be available for issue in n+1.
When the last write beat of a burst issues in cycle t, o_bvalid shall be asserted in t+1; for a single-beat write the minimum AW handshake → o_bvalid latency shall be c3.

For a read issued in cycle t (o_sram_oe in t), the SRAM data shall be sampled and pushed into RFIFO in t+1 and o_rvalid shall be asserted in t+2; the minimum AR handshake → first o_rvalid latency shall be c4.
Reads shall issue at most once per 2 cycles (0.5 beat/cycle) independent of PARA_NUM_BANKS; with continuous back-to-back reads and RFIFO never full, reads shall issue every 2 cycles.
Writes shall be able to issue at up to 1 beat per cycle.

Each address FSM shall generate 1 beat per cycle while its FIFO is not full; for a burst with AxLEN = L and no back-pressure it shall push in c1…c(L+1), hold AxREADY = 0 in c1…c(L+2) and be able to accept the next burst in c(L+3) (minimum interval AxLEN + 3 cycles).
C1: PARA_DATA_WD shall be a multiple of 8 with a power-of-two number of byte lanes: PARA_DATA_WD % 8 == 0 && ((PARA_DATA_WD/8) & (PARA_DATA_WD/8 - 1)) == 0.
C2: PARA_DATA_WD shall be within 8 … 1024: PARA_DATA_WD >= 8 && PARA_DATA_WD <= 1024.
C3: PARA_FIFO_DEPTH shall be a power of 2 and at least 2: PARA_FIFO_DEPTH >= 2 && (PARA_FIFO_DEPTH & (PARA_FIFO_DEPTH - 1)) == 0.
C4: PARA_NUM_BANKS shall be a power of 2 and at least 1: PARA_NUM_BANKS >= 1 && (PARA_NUM_BANKS & (PARA_NUM_BANKS - 1)) == 0.
C5: with multiple banks the address shall be wide enough for the bank hash: PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1 -> PARA_ADDR_WD >= BYTE_LSB + $clog2(PARA_NUM_BANKS).
C6: PARA_ADDR_WD shall be wider than the byte offset: PARA_ADDR_WD > BYTE_LSB.
C7: PARA_ID_WD shall be at least 1: PARA_ID_WD >= 1.
C8: PARA_LEN_WD shall be within 1 … 8: PARA_LEN_WD >= 1 && PARA_LEN_WD <= 8.

The design shall meet a target i_clk frequency of 100 MHz (10 ns period) at the default parameters, checked in synthesis: the combinational issue path (FIFO head → request generation, bank hash and arbitration → SRAM control/data outputs) and the READY paths shall fit within one cycle without adding pipeline stages or changing the specified cycle behaviour.

parameters.name: PARA_DATA_WD
parameters.description: AXI and SRAM data width in bits; PARA_DATA_WD/8 byte lanes (width of i_wstrb/o_sram_wstrb).

parameters.name: PARA_ADDR_WD
parameters.description: AXI byte-address width and o_sram_addr width.

parameters.name: PARA_LEN_WD
parameters.description: Width of i_awlen/i_arlen; maximum burst 2**PARA_LEN_WD beats.

parameters.name: PARA_FIFO_DEPTH
parameters.description: Number of entries in each of the five FIFOs.

parameters.name: PARA_NUM_BANKS
parameters.description: Number of independent SRAM banks; 1 = single-SRAM behaviour.

constraints.description: Data width is a whole number of bytes with a power-of-two lane count.
FIFO depth is a power of 2, at least 2.
Bank count is a power of 2.
Address wide enough for the bank hash (BYTE_LSB = $clog2(PARA_DATA_WD/8)).
Address wider than the byte offset (BYTE_LSB).

modules.name: m_vlsi_axi4_sram
modules.description: Top level: instantiates and wires all sub-modules (u_vlsi_axfsm_0/1, u_vlsi_fifo_0..4, u_vlsi_arbiter, u_vlsi_sram_misc); owns all ports.

modules.name: m_vlsi_axfsm
modules.description: AXI address FSM: handshake, burst address generation sized by AxSIZE, alignment/oversize error detection, pushes {last, err, id, addr} into its FIFO.

modules.name: m_vlsi_fifo
modules.description: Parameterised synchronous FIFO with extra-MSB full/empty detection.

modules.name: m_vlsi_arbiter
modules.description: Shared round-robin toggle arbiter between write and read requests.

modules.name: m_vlsi_sram_misc
modules.description: Structural wrapper instantiating u_vlsi_axi_fifopack, u_vlsi_bank_arb and u_vlsi_sram_fanout.

modules.name: m_vlsi_axi_fifopack
modules.description: Combinational FIFO pack/unpack, err→SLVERR substitution, R/B output unpacking, read-bank rdata mux into RFIFO.

modules.name: m_vlsi_bank_arb
modules.description: Request generation, bank XOR hash, grant/issue decision, FIFO push/pop control and o_wready.

modules.name: m_vlsi_sram_fanout
modules.description: Per-bank SRAM control/data fan-out (we/wstrb gating for SLVERR) and the one-cycle read pipeline register.
